title: Fig and pear crumble with hazelnuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Fruit, butter, flour, oats, sugar, honey, hazelnuts and Greek yoghurt are all ordinary home staples.

supermarket.reason: Figs, pears and hazelnuts are all on mainstream supermarket shelves in October at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, a bowl and fingertip rubbing-in, which suits a beginner.

works.reason: Eight figs and three pears under a 100g flour, 75g butter and 50g oat topping at 190°C for 30 to 35 minutes gives a properly baked crumble for four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers quartering figs, coring and chopping pears, chopping nuts and rubbing in, and the 35-minute bake matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon and both halves of the cinnamon, is used, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm fig and pear crumble suits late October, and the figs are central to the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is mostly fruit with oats, nuts and yoghurt and only modest added sugar, a satisfying snack a family would make again.
